title: Mix and deliver feedlot feed to bunker

lessons.title: Getting ready to mix feed
lessons.html:
Your job in the feedlot

In a feedlot the cattle eat only what we give them. If the feed is wrong, late or badly mixed, the cattle grow slowly or get sick. Your job is to mix the right feed and put it in the right bunker at the right time.

The feed sheet

Every day the bunk reader or supervisor gives you a feed sheet. It tells you:

  • which ration to mix, for example the starter ration or the finisher ration;
  • how many kilograms of each ingredient go into the mixer;
  • which pens get the feed and how many kilograms each pen gets;
  • the time of each feeding.

Read the feed sheet carefully. If you do not understand it, ask before you start. Never change the amounts yourself.

Check the machines

Before you start, walk around the tractor and the mixer wagon.

  1. Check oil, water and fuel in the tractor.
  2. Check the tyres.
  3. Check that all guards are in place, especially over the PTO shaft.
  4. Check the scale on the mixer. It must show zero when the mixer is empty.
  5. Look inside the mixer for old feed, wire, stones or tools. Do this only when the engine is off and the key is in your pocket.

Check the ingredients

Look at the feed in the store: maize meal, hay, silage, molasses, protein and the premix. Is it dry? Is there mould? Does it smell bad? Mouldy or wet feed can make cattle sick. Do not use it. Tell your supervisor.

lessons.title: Loading and mixing the ration
lessons.html:
Load in the right order

The feed must be mixed the same way every time. Follow the loading order that your feedlot uses. Often it is like this:

  1. Long roughage first, like chopped hay.
  2. Then grain, like maize meal.
  3. Then small amounts, like the premix or protein.
  4. Wet feeds, like silage and molasses, last.

Weigh carefully

Watch the scale as you load. Stop when the scale shows the amount on the feed sheet. A little too much or too little of the premix can be dangerous, because premix often contains salt, minerals and products that must be fed in the right amount. Write down the real amount you loaded for each ingredient.

Mix for the right time

Run the mixer for the time your supervisor tells you, usually a few minutes after the last ingredient goes in. Too short and the feed is not mixed well. Too long and the hay breaks into dust. A good mix looks the same all through, with no lumps of meal or balls of hay.

Stay safe

  • Never climb into or onto the mixer when the PTO is turning.
  • Never put your hand into the augers. They can pull off your arm.
  • Before you clean or fix the mixer, stop the engine, take out the key and wait until everything stops.
  • Wear a dust mask when you handle dusty feed and premix.
  • Keep other people away from the loader and the tractor.

If something breaks, stop the machine and tell your supervisor. Do not try to fix it while it is running.

lessons.title: Delivering feed to the bunker
lessons.html:
Putting feed in the bunker

Drive slowly to the pens. Check the pen number on the feed sheet. Feeding the wrong pen is a serious mistake: young cattle may get finisher feed that is too strong and they can get sick with bloat or acidosis.

How to deliver

  1. Drive along the bunker at an even speed so the feed is spread evenly.
  2. Watch the scale. Give each pen exactly the kilograms on the feed sheet.
  3. Do not drop feed on the road or into the water trough.
  4. Write down the time and the kilograms for each pen.

Feed on time

Cattle like to eat at the same time every day. If feed comes late, they get hungry and then eat too fast, and some can get sick. Keep to the times on the feed sheet.

Look at the cattle and the bunker

While you feed, look. Tell your supervisor if you see:

  • a bunker that is still full of old feed, or one that is licked clean;
  • wet, mouldy or dirty feed in the bunker;
  • a sick animal, for example one lying down, with a swollen left side, or not coming to eat;
  • a broken water trough or a broken fence.

After feeding

Park the tractor and mixer in the right place. Switch off and take the key. Clean spilt feed. Hand in your feed sheet with the amounts written down.

Key points

  • Always follow the feed sheet and never change the amounts yourself.
  • Load ingredients in the right order and weigh each one carefully.
  • Never touch the mixer or augers while the PTO is turning.
  • Feed the right pen, the right amount, at the right time.
  • Report sick cattle, bad feed and problems to your supervisor.
